native_result.query: In which domain do the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies with ratio of males in original and replication studies being and 0.87 and 0.84 respectively.
native_result.HypoB: Economics (experimental economics — the same block as replication project `ee`, 18 original/replication pairs) is the domain in which the majority of authors tend to be male for BOTH original and replication studies. Pooling the actual people inside the domain: originals 42/48 = 87.5% male, replications 48/59 = 81.4% male — both strictly above 0.5 (margins +0.375 and +0.314). All four metrics agree and so does the tie handling: share of pairs with a male author majority 77.8% (14/18) originals and 72.2% (13/18) replications, mean male ratio 0.870 vs 0.837, median 1.00 vs 1.00, and only 4 (o) / 2 (r) of 18 pairs sit exactly at 0.5. Economics is the ONLY discipline that passes >0.5 on both sides under all four metrics in all three unit-of-analysis variants. The psychology disciplines do not: Social (n=74) 64.8% vs 53.4%, Cognitive (n=49) 70.6% vs 51.9% — margins +0.034 and +0.019 — and both fail as soon as the metric is 'share of pairs with a male-majority team' (48.7%, 44.9%) or the median pair (exactly 0.5 = tie); their margin comes entirely from the Many Labs consortium teams (ml1 0.560 of 51 authors, ml3 0.516 of 64), and counting each team once per project pushes Social to 49.4% and Cognitive to 50.3%, while Economics stays at 81.4%. The project cut points at the identical block ee (0.875 vs 0.814), rpp fails outright (0.649 vs 0.460), and ml1/ml3 clear 0.5 only degenerately (one shared consortium team behind all their studies). So discipline and project converge on Economics/ee as the domain where authorship is male-majority on both sides. Main caveat: original and replication author sets are two different groups of people, and for Many Labs 1/3 the replication side is a single 51-/64-author consortium rather than per-study teams.
native_result.WorkflowB: Descriptive only (no models, no tests, replicated/relative_es unused). (1) Inspect file1 (927x57, 141 unique O/R ids, 135 original studies, 0 missing in authors_male.*, 312/75 ratios exactly 0.5, no authors.r column, ee==Economics 1:1). (2) file2 (143x15) NOT used: no author-gender column and no join key (study vs title/authors.o overlap = 0). (3) Primary metric per domain per side = SUM(authors_male*n_authors)/SUM(n_authors); secondary = share of pairs with ratio>0.5, mean and median of pair ratios, count of 0.5 ties; threshold strictly >0.5, 0.5 = tie. (4) Three unit variants: (a) one row per id with aggregated row for ml1/ml3 [primary, n=141], (b) all 927 rows [naive/contaminated], (c) unit-level excluding drop==True [n=131]. (5) Both taxonomies (discipline headline, project parallel) + discipline x project crosstab + metric-by-domain pass matrix + consortium-concentration diagnostics. (6) Headline numbers re-derived independently from integer author counts (42/48, 48/59). (7) Gender taken only from supplied ratio columns, no name-based inference.
